questions: For the due date function (the date n business days after a start date): which days count as non-business days — only Saturdays and Sundays, or also public holidays? If holidays count, whose holiday calendar (which country or region) and who maintains the list?

For the due date function: if the start date itself falls on a weekend or holiday, does counting begin from the next business day, and is the start day itself ever counted as day zero or day one? For example, an invoice dated Friday with 1 business day — is it due Monday?

For the due date function: what should happen when the number of business days is zero, negative, fractional, blank or not a number — return the start date, count backwards, round, or reject it with an error?

For the due date function: what should happen when the start date is blank, missing, in an unrecognised format (for example 03/04/2026), an impossible date (31 February), or includes a time or time zone — reject it, or accept and interpret it a certain way?
For the late-payment fee: is the fee a flat amount, a percentage of the overdue invoice, or a mix (for example a percentage with a minimum)? What are the actual amounts or rates?

For the late-payment fee: is there a grace period after the due date during which no fee is charged, and is an invoice paid exactly on the due date, or exactly on the last grace day, treated as on time?
For the late-payment fee: does the fee grow the longer the invoice is overdue (for example per day, per week or per month, or in tiers such as 1–30 days and 31–60 days), or is it charged once only?
For the late-payment fee: is there a minimum fee and a maximum cap (for example never more than 25% of the invoice or never more than a set amount)? What are they?
For the late-payment fee: when a percentage gives a fraction of a cent, should it round to the nearest cent, always up, or always down?

For the late-payment fee: what should happen for an invoice that is not overdue, is partly paid (is the fee based on the full amount or the unpaid balance), has a zero or negative amount (such as a credit note), or has a missing amount or due date?
For masking a payment card number: how many digits are left visible and which ones — the last four only, or also the first six? Which character replaces the hidden digits?

For masking a payment card number: should the masked result keep the original spacing or dashes, or be shown in a fixed layout such as groups of four? Should the length of the masked number match the original card length?
For masking a payment card number: what should happen if the input contains spaces, dashes or other non-digit characters — strip them before masking, or keep them?

For masking a payment card number: what should happen if the number is blank, missing, or too short to mask safely (for example fewer than 8 digits) or unusually long — show nothing, mask everything, or reject it?

For the percentage change between two period figures: what should be shown when the earlier (base) figure is zero — a blank, 0%, 100%, 'n/a', or an error? Does it matter whether the new figure is also zero?
For the percentage change: how many decimal places should the result show, and should it round to nearest, up or down? Is it returned as a number (12.5) or as text with a percent sign?

For the percentage change: when the earlier figure is negative (for example a loss turning into a smaller loss), should the change be measured against the absolute value of the earlier figure so that an improvement shows as positive, or use the plain formula?
For the percentage change: what should happen when either figure is missing, blank or not a number — show blank, treat it as zero, or reject it?
For the fiscal quarter label: in which month does the fiscal year start (January, April, July, October, or something else)?

For the fiscal quarter label: is the fiscal year named after the calendar year in which it starts or the one in which it ends (for example, is a quarter in November 2026 for a year starting in July part of FY2026 or FY2027)?
For the fiscal quarter label: what exact format should the label take — for example 'Q1 FY2027', 'FY27-Q1', or '2027 Q1'? Two-digit or four-digit year?
For the fiscal quarter label: do the quarters follow calendar months exactly, or does the company use a 4-4-5 / 52-week calendar where quarters start and end on particular weekdays?

For the fiscal quarter label: what should happen if the date is blank, missing, in an unrecognised format, includes a time or time zone, or is outside a sensible range (for example before 2000 or far in the future)?
For the shipping charge: what are the weight bands and prices for each delivery zone? Please provide the rate table, including which zones exist.

For the shipping charge: at an exact band boundary (for example exactly 1 kg when bands are up to 1 kg and 1–2 kg) which band applies? In what unit is the weight given (grams, kilograms, pounds, ounces)?
For the shipping charge: should the weight be rounded up to the next whole unit (for example the next 100 g or 0.5 kg) before pricing, or is the exact weight used? Which rounding direction?
For the shipping charge: is there a minimum charge, and what happens above the heaviest band — a per-unit surcharge, a flat cap, or are such parcels refused?
For the shipping charge: what should happen when the weight is zero, negative, blank or not a number? Should a zero-weight parcel ship free, pay the minimum, or be rejected?

For the shipping charge: what should happen for an unknown, blank or oddly formatted delivery zone (for example lowercase, extra spaces) — treat it as a default zone, ignore case and spaces, or reject it?

For the shipping charge: are there other adjustments such as fuel surcharges, remote-area fees, free shipping above an order value, or dimensional weight, or is the charge based only on weight and zone?
For the voucher code made from a numeric id: which characters may appear in the code (digits only, or letters too), and should look-alike characters such as 0/O and 1/I/L be excluded?
For the voucher code: how long should the code be — fixed length padded to a set number of characters, or as short as the id allows? What should happen when the id is too large for the fixed length?
For the voucher code: should the code be uppercase only, and should it be split into groups with dashes (for example ABCD-EFGH)? Should it include a check character to catch typing mistakes?
For the voucher code: must the same id always produce the same code, and should codes be hard to guess (scrambled) or can they simply follow the id order?
For the voucher code: what should happen when the id is zero, negative, fractional, blank or not a number — produce a code, or reject it?

For the web slug from a title: which characters are kept — only lowercase letters and digits, or also accented letters? Should accented letters be converted to plain ones (é to e) and what happens to letters from non-Latin alphabets (Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic)?
For the web slug: what separator replaces spaces and punctuation (a hyphen or something else), and should repeated separators collapse into one and leading or trailing separators be removed?

For the web slug: should the text be forced to lowercase? Should symbols such as '&', '%' or '@' be dropped or spelled out ('and', 'percent', 'at')? What about apostrophes — 'Bob's' becomes 'bobs' or 'bob-s'?
For the web slug: is there a maximum length, and if so where is a long title cut — at the exact limit or at the last whole word?

For the web slug: what should be returned when the title is blank, missing, or contains nothing usable after cleaning (for example only symbols) — an empty slug, a default such as 'untitled', or an error? Should it ever add a number to keep slugs unique?

For the customer-facing star rating label: what are the label wordings and the score ranges for each (for example 4.5 and above is 'Excellent')? Where exactly are the cut-offs, and does a score exactly on a cut-off get the higher label?
For the star rating label: is the rating on a 1–5 scale, and is it rounded to the nearest whole or half star before choosing the label? Which rounding direction applies at exact halves?
For the star rating label: should products with very few reviews get a special label such as 'Not yet rated' instead of a rating label? What is the minimum number of reviews?

For the star rating label: what should be shown if the rating is blank, missing, below the lowest or above the highest allowed value, or not a number — a blank, 'Not yet rated', or the nearest valid label? Is a zero rating valid?
For the average of numeric values in a group: should blank or missing entries be skipped (not counted) or treated as zero?

For the average: how should text that cannot be read as a number be handled, and what about text that looks like a number such as '12' or '1,200' or '$5' — skip it, convert it, or reject the whole group?
For the average: what should be shown when the group is empty or has no numeric values — zero, blank, 'n/a', or an error?
For the average: how many decimal places should the result have and should it round to nearest, up or down? Should negative values and zeros be included normally?
For the average: should extreme outliers ever be excluded, and should the group be limited to a certain period or can all values be included?
